about: Every number the text cites, with its source and evidence state. Sources: terluna:<path> at commit 186b294, repo:<path> in this repository, drive:<path> on Terluna's research drive, calc:<text>. States: observation, calculation, conditional model, calibration, reproduction, identity, sensitivity, documented, finding.

claims.text: The scenario: 1.2 atm of N2 and O2 at the water level, seas and lakes over 28% of the surface, shield-filtered sunlight, g 1.62 m/s2, a 29.53-day solar day
The lunar column holds 7.25 times Earth's air per square metre (74,861 against 10,332 kg/m2)
Scale height about 52 km against a 1,737 km radius, H/R about 23 times Earth's; horizon air mass from 35 to about 7
One Earth day after sunset the Sun stands 12.2 deg down and the geometric shadow 40.1 km up, with 0.465 of an isothermal column's mass above it and 0.45 of the design profile's; refraction ignored
121,590 Pa at the water level; O2 21,227 Pa (17.5%); Earth's Ar/N2; 400 ppm CO2; global mean 1.16 atm, range 1.02-1.22 atm (A28_corrected_970, year 19)
Seas at 28% of the surface; with rain-fed lakes, 759 of the GCM's 2,048 cells, 40% of its surface, are water
TSIS-1 through the titania shield: 1,235 W/m2 at the top of the air, dimmed to 1,198 W/m2 (scale 0.970) in the design case; no ozone behind the shield
Column water vapour 170 kg/m2 in the design case and 348 kg/m2 in the longwave-and-ice test (years 15-19 of each); Earth about 25
Mass-mean height 48.6 km; a shell there has 5.7% more area than the ground beneath it; horizon air mass 7.1 for air and 13.5 for water against PlaSim's 35

Gravity at the 86 km tropopause 9% below the surface's; a constant-area column with falling gravity holds about 5% more air than p_s/g_s (5.3% on the design profile; 5.5% on the ledger's moist column), and the spherical shells 11.5% more per square metre of ground (84,876 against 76,096 kg/m2)
Pressure levels six times higher; droplets 6.04x, rain 2.94x, graupel 2.27x slower; sea roughness 6.04x longer; deep-water waves 0.41 of Earth's speed

The dry dynamics stretch about sixfold in size and duration, so a 6 km column stands for about 1 km at Earth's scale; the microphysics and radiation do not stretch; the gravity pair, designed to measure how far lunar convection departs from Earth's stretched sixfold, failed to convect
Soil thermal wave about 0.6 m deep, 5.4 times Earth's diurnal depth; Coriolis 5.2e-6 /s at 80 deg, inertial period 14 days

CM1 sets g = 9.81 in constants.F, module_ra_etc.F, getcape.F and morrison.F on the lunar paths, and in schemes the lunar cases leave unselected; Morrison's fall-speed laws and caps hold Earth's gravity
WRF-ELEC's NSSL sets gr = 9.8 twice and ties rain and ice ventilation to Earth's fall-speed coefficients
Breakdown cap 180 kV/m acts below ~4.5 km on Earth and ~36 km in lunar air (-44% at the ground); -7 C ground-strike level 5 km on Earth, 27-34 km on the Moon; 0.75 s sub-step for 500 m layers
SWAN's AGROW knee fixed at 1 Hz, called mostly arbitrary in its comments; stock SWAN misses the sixfold similarity test by 5.44% in Hs
SWAN fixes air density at 1.28 kg/m3; CM1's air over the equatorial seas averages 1.40390 kg/m3
RRTMG sets CO2 by calendar year and carries Earth's CH4, N2O, halocarbons and ozone; CM1's beta plane uses Earth's rotation and a 6,370 km radius

Slingo's convective cover converts rain with the model's solar day (zrfac = solar_day*1000), a unit conversion that ExoPlaSim's replacement of the solar day by 86,400 s in its unit conversions (Paradise et al. 2022, Sect. 2.1) left in place: a defect; 29.8 Earth days for the Moon, rain read 30x too heavy, cover +0.42; bias 0.125 ln(day) on any world
ExoPlaSim's 360-day year of 17,280 steps holds 12.08 lunar model days of 1,430 steps; output slips 120 steps a year
CM1's Sun follows Earth's day, calendar and a 23.5 deg obliquity (radconst); soil layers 1-16 cm; the lunar thermal wave about 0.6 m
WRF-ELEC carries no clear-air conduction (its screening option acts only at cloud edges); in a month-long lunar run ion charge persisted for weeks, holding ~20 kV/m at the ground

Against the same air in flat layers (with a pseudo-spherical direct beam for the sunlight), the curved geometry takes in 10.3 W/m2 more sunlight and lets out 16.2 W/m2 more infrared, 5.8 net: shells' widening -6.5, curved light and escape +0.7; twilight 1.4 W/m2 on the ground
PlaSim's horizon magnification 35/sqrt(1 + 1224 mu^2); the Moon's factor 13.5 for water and 7.1 for air
PlaSim's thin shell and CM1's flat slab hold g constant; reference models use GM/r^2; g 5.4% lower at 48.6 km and 15.3% at 150 km
Lacis-Hansen water absorptivity left the air absorbing 7.7-8.2 points too little on 11 columns

Rayleigh normalised to a 5772 K blackbody gives too low a coefficient for the filtered Sun; TH2OC over-absorbs; the uncalibrated first design run (25% seas, undimmed shield) passed 310 K, 315.5 K at model year 12
PlaSim's two shortwave bands omit CO2 and O2; the calibrated water multiplier took their share lower down

PlaSim's longwave (Sasamori's absorptivities, with a water continuum the first calibration fitted to OLR) cools the lowest two layers 9.7-11.9 W/m2 too much and the air aloft up to 12 W/m2 too little against correlated-k
CCM3 cloud water falls off on 700 ln(1+PW) m of geometric height; lunar cloud above ~20 km left nearly dry
Liquid optics for all cloud; saturation over liquid sets the threshold, so high cloud at 180-204 K in the second layer from the top forms only at 136-149% of ice saturation
RRTMG reference pressures begin at 1,053.63 hPa; the lowest 7.4-7.5 km over the sea are extrapolated in ln p; ice optics end at 140 um; the box stopped at day 6.45 at 157 um

Morrison as CM1 carries it bounds rain's mean diameter at 2.8 mm and begins breakup above 0.3 mm (breakup added after Verlinde and Cotton 1993, morrison.F line 27); the capillary length is 2.46x longer at lunar g

Retained Earth calibrations: Wu drag, Komen, the AGROW coefficient, breaker index 0.73 (Battjes and Stive 1985), SWASH breaking 0.6/0.3, the charging laws (Takahashi's inverts the lunar storms' arrangement of charge)

solang turns the Sun at the rotation rate and restarts each model day in non-synchronous runs on the default solar geometry: skip 1/(N-1) of a turn, none at ExoPlaSim's default one-day rotation, ~1 deg for a rotation near Earth's set away from one day, 10 deg at ten days, ~16 deg at 12-20 days and ~33 deg for slower rotations, where the wrapper sets N = 12; 32.5 deg a day on the Moon, sunlight 8.3% short at 270-57 E and up to 17% over near 164 E
The fixedorbit default puts Earth's orbit for 1 AD (23.695 deg) in place of the configured one: 149 against 29 W/m2 at 86 deg; summer rain to 60 deg
SWAN reads KTETA uninitialised with breaking off; repeated Earth runs differed ~2.5% in Hs; hidden with breaking on

CM1 on several threads parts at 3,000-7,400 s, first in total vertical momentum, in the plain Morrison box too; since every patch in a threaded region writes only its own points, the race lies in CM1's own threaded loops; unlocated
PlaSim's lowest level reads up to ~20 K too cold in 0.8% of 3-day windows, most likely from the spectral transform over steep terrain
The runner's held infrared tail put 86% of sunlight in the near infrared and warmed the first run past 320 K

First electrified build: field a median 3.2x breakdown at discharge, 150 C removed; uninitialised scaling and a privatised variable caught by thread-count changes; ventilation missed, rain evaporating 1.3-1.5x too fast

The sky model's 114 production channels absorbed 104.5 W/m2 above 500 nm against the fine grid's 66.2 (58% too much); the ledger's first channels put near-IR sunlight too high (19.0 against 10.7 W/m2 at 66-85 km), and the two 20-year curved-air GCM tests ran on those terms

Terrain forcing by a corner column at 2.9 km; constant vapour above the GCM's top level near 130 km, the 45 N rings 6-15x ice-saturated at 140-150 km and holding 1.1 g/m2 of ice above 107 km in every column through both lunar days; the 45 N twilight pair on -O2 and -O3 builds, its 0.013-0.021 K effect below what the pair resolves
The first box rained in the mornings and was stopped at day 47; at 45 N the missing sideways transport is about a third of CM1's warm offset

Ten ExoPlaSim patches, each with a namelist switch written to reproduce the released code at its default (identity run for five); CM1 gravity, CO2 and O2 as preprocessor constants and var1-var20; the patch series generated from the runners' edit lists
V = aD^b scales as g^((b+1)/3): droplets 6.04x, rain 2.94x, graupel 2.27x slower at lunar gravity
Rayleigh damping x g/9.81 and l_inf x 9.81/g; WRF-ELEC sub-step 0.75 -> 6.8 s keeps graupel settling ~1% of a 2 km layer at 0.44 of Earth's speed; the boxes run one 8 s sub-step per step
SWAN's knee at f g_E/g reproduces stock SWAN at standard gravity (9.80665, set by input) and restores gravity similarity (sixfold test 5.44% -> 0.303% in Hs)

The curved-air table: one clear design column (1.2 atm, 205 kg/m2 water, 294.9 K surface, 100 shells); 10,697 channels bisected within bands until each absorbs a direct beam within 1% of its sunlight as its members do and above 1,250 nm keeps the beam's loss by layer; single channels below 500 nm; 282 scattering channels by successive orders (cap 100); beam channels with pseudo-spherical two-stream diffuse light; shell widening -6.5 W/m2 net, curved light and escape +0.7
Terms at 167 elevations from -40 to 90 deg for PlaSim layers and CM1 shells, infrared escape scaled with T^4; slant fits within 0.30% (water) and 0.08% (air)
With the Sun overhead the spherical solver's ground takes 1.3% less than the two-stream's: part of the daytime term is a solver difference

The reference: line-by-line on HITRAN lines as served 2026-09-24 (HITRAN2020 or later), MT_CKD 4.3, CIA, Rayleigh, g = GM/r^2, pseudo-spherical beam; correlated-k OLR within 0.4 W/m2 at 288-290 K and 1.4 W/m2 for a saturated 330 K lunar column; its correlated-k tables span 0.1 Pa to 3.2e5 Pa and 100-375 K and clamp at their edges

First calibration: albedo within ~0.007 and OLR within ~2 W/m2; when the Sun-clock and orbit faults were found, the split showed the air 7.7-8.2 points short, and with the repair the water multiplier brought it within 0.3 points rms on 11 columns
PlaSim put ~nothing above 85 km against line-by-line's 4.2 W/m2; three gas bands within 0.13% of band energy; layers 1.71 -> 0.97 W/m2 rms
The longwave correction, fitted on ~2,100 cloud-free 3-day means over land and sea and scaled with T^4, removes each layer's mean error, leaving 1-5 W/m2 column to column

Ice optics below -38 C (Ebert-Curry, delta two-stream, Kristjansson-Mitchell radius); the WRF-ELEC graft: NSSL with charge, FFT/tridiagonal Poisson solver, cylindrical and branched lightning on a wrapping domain, screening

Leakage through a computed conductivity column and a condition for ground strikes: a channel reaching the -7 C level counts only if its potential carries a leader to the ground at 1 kV/m internal field at sea-level density, scaled with density, placing ground strikes between the stopping-field and -7 C bounds; point discharge ran in one window and is off in the lunar runs
Ring columns each with their own Sun (a box takes one) and Coriolis on tilted rings; nudging only above 8-16 km; the GCM's vertical wind through CM1's large-scale advection

Local-time heating and moistening; terrain forcing by column height; SWAN forced by GCM stress through an inverted Wu law, its friction velocity within -2.5 to +1.2% of the GCM's; spherical at the lunar radius, band scaled by g/g_E; SWASH unmodified

Five ExoPlaSim identity runs repeat the restart of the same build before the patch; the chain to the released model closes for patches 01-03, and the infrared and ice-optics checks compared against builds with patches 04, 05 (and 07-09) not yet run at their off settings; the water scaling's identity at its default follows from arithmetic on this spectrum; kill-and-resume restart identical, output identical in 39 variables, 12 header bytes differ

CM1 tilted-ring patches and local-time advection repeat a first model day bit for bit; single-thread runs repeat; the electrified supercell restarted on 4 and 2 threads repeats fields and 41 flashes; SWAN with the wind-input patch equals stock at standard gravity

The series rebuild byte for byte the deployed ExoPlaSim copy's two patched sources and the Fortran of eight lunar CM1 builds, and moon_omp's sources are byte-identical to moon_omp_o3's; the Earth-gravity benchmark builds came from earlier states; ExoPlaSim prefixes reproduce 32 of 34 hashed GCM runs; the uncalibrated and first calibrated runs predate hashing and the convective-cover run compiled a draft of patch 03 whose committed form repeats its first year
SWAN sixfold similarity: stock 5.44% (Hs) and 3.91% (Tm); patched 0.303% and 0.326% against a 1% criterion; largest peak-period difference one bin
SWASH: dispersion within 1.76% amplitude and 0.289% phase at three gravities; linear similarity 0.000908%; run-up within 1.20% under gravity and clock scaling with breaking
The CM1 gravity pair (pair_moon, pair_earth), designed to measure how far lunar convection departs from Earth's stretched sixfold, failed to convect

Clear-sky split within 0.6 points rms on 11 columns outside the fit; at 0 E the air takes 31.4% as line-by-line's does; a 303 K, 338 kg/m2 column 0.7 points short against 9.7 before the water recalibration
RRTMG within 2.5 points at the crossing; on 990 cloud-free 45 N columns it cools 4.5, 8.5 and 10.2 W/m2 more than correlated-k at 0-1.8, 1.8-6.5 and 6.5-13.7 km
Electrified supercell against CM1's NSSL: updrafts within 6%, reflectivity 3.4 dBZ at every half hour, condensate 9%, graupel 12% from 30 min, hail within a factor of two

Against published electrification: first flash 28.5 min (27-40); rates and median charge per flash in range; with the ground rule on 1.1% ground strikes against 0.33% published; charging several times stronger from cloud ice up to 2e8 per kg

Arithmetic checks: solang rebuild correlation 1.0000; Sun within 8e-7 and Coriolis within 3e-12 /s; field solver 1 part in 1e5; ledger channels within 0.9 W/m2 per layer with the Sun overhead; positive conductivity within 2-8% at 5-30 km at a 3 GV cutoff
SWAN breaking off: ~2.5% repeat difference; early growth up to 33% with the time step, endpoints under 0.3%; small seas fail 5%; SWASH irregular input 5.22% and 6.28%
CM1 -O3 rebuild 0.28-0.32 C rms at 2 m within a day; one ledger channel of 282 at the 100-order cap, omitted tail ~3e-4 of its ground diffuse field

Missing checks: the full design column through an independent radiation code; CM1 from the longwave-corrected GCM; the longwave fit at 307 K; the twilight pair's control; RRTMG's extrapolation; the unlocated thread race; CM1 microphysics similarity; an independent GCM
On run A (25% seas, undimmed shield): cloud water by pressure +2.30 K over the averaged years, ~2.5 K settled; convective cover per Earth day +1.76 K, ~1.6 K settled

Sun clock, tilt and split (one step from A28_dim5): +0.59 K; rain 2.91 -> 2.24 mm/day; land under 0.5 mm/day 9% -> 42%, 36% within two years of the Sun and tilt alone; with Earth's 23.7 deg tilt summer rain had reached 60 deg

Curved air -0.65 K, clouds returning 3.5 of the clear sky's 5.4 W/m2 in the first year; gas bands -2.23 K, a cloud-free column moving only 0.57 K, the high deck 16.2% -> 11.6% and the top layer's cirrus 2.0% -> 0.05% as it warmed 7 K

With the curved air on the ledger's corrected terms and the gas bands, at a sunlight scale of 0.970 (3.0% dimming, eased from 5%), the design case settles at 295.02 K with 2.31 mm/day; the scale was chosen to hold the design temperature

Cloud-setting effects, window means and settled: thinner convective cloud +1.71 K, ~+2.2 K settled; more low cloud -4.98 K, ~-5.9 K; full-column cloud water -3.21 K, ~-3.5 K on the first calibrated run; longwave correction with ice +11.5 K over years 10-19 toward ~307 K, vapour 348 against 170 kg/m2, cloud cover 38% against 20%, most of the gain high
45 N ring: lowest 1.8 km 5.9 K above the GCM; the imposed transport (~15 W/m2 out of the air below 8 km) cuts it to 3.7 K

Against correlated-k, PlaSim's longwave cools its lowest layer 10.6 W/m2 too much on 151 cloud-free 3-day means at 47 N and RRTMG CM1's lowest 1.8 km 4.5 W/m2 too much: ~6 W/m2, ~1.5 K of the 3.7 K at the ring's estimated 4 W/m2 per K; at the 0 E crossing on A28_dim5 forcing (12% too little sunlight), a 3-D box ran warmer, land at most 0.3 C, Earth-speed rain +1.0 C, each a pair of realisations; the remainder, a degree or two, attributed by elimination to boundary-layer transport

The small box on pre-correction forcing: 34 mm per lunar day at the ground against the forcing GCM's 129 mm and the corrected GCM's 180 mm; 85% of falling water evaporated against 64% at Earth's fall speeds

Over the second lunar day of six Morrison runs (three boxes at 0 E forced from A28_dim5, one with Earth's fall speeds; three rings forced from A28_dim5_moon) the 0 C level stands near 25 km and -40 C near 60 km, five to six times their heights in Earth's tropics; cloud tops 55-80 km

Main electrified run, two lunar days of a box at 0 E forced from A28_dim5: 530 flashes, at most a fifth negative to ground under the condition for ground strikes, none positive; 0.022 per km2 per year, about a hundredth (0.0081) of Earth's 2.72 from 44 flashes/s; start 35.8 km; 108 C in cloud, 149 C to ground; main negative charge 40-42 km at -13 to -14 C; hail 87% of non-inductive charging; on the Earth benchmark a coarser grid gave fewer, larger flashes

In two windows of an earlier electrified run (days 10.5-12 and 40.5-42, before the ventilation repair, leakage off) Takahashi's law separates as much charge as Saunders and Peck's, within the spread of the Saunders and Peck runs, with the storms' arrangement of charge inverted (main negative charge above the positive); the windows' ground strikes, all negative under both laws, carried charge left over from the run without leakage; NSSL's main run against Morrison's box: 1.0 C warmer at 2 m, night ground fog 29% against 56% of the box, one realisation against another

With Wu's drag at both gravities the same 10 m wind, fetch and duration build waves 4-5x as high and periods 5x as long as Earth's; Charnock's roughness at each gravity would raise the ratio 11-51%; median 10 m wind 2.6 m/s over the equatorial seas; nearside sea 5.29 million km2, mean Hs 1.39 m, 68% >= 1 m, largest 4.9 m (19.3 s); run-up 2.1 m (98th percentile) at the western Smythii face; one measured lunar cycle after a spin-up

General repairs (Sun clock, cover per Earth day, cloud water by pressure, CM1 gravity and fall speeds, CM1's Sun and soil, breakdown cap, sub-step, damping and mixing length, flash-reach logging, SWAN's knee, ice optics within range) built to apply unchanged; fixed orbit and whole model days are avoidances; leakage and the forcing methods read their inputs; the condition for ground strikes is a bound; the curved-air terms are a method with a per-world table; the calibrations (Rayleigh, water multiplier, continuum, longwave correction, gas fits) hold near their case

Chapman factors 22 (Mars), 24.5 (Venus), 14 (Titan), 7.2 (Moon); columns 10x, 100x, 7.25x Earth's; Slingo bias 0.35 at 16 d and 0.60 at 117 d; Sun-clock skip 1/(N-1) turn with N rounded to a multiple of 12 and never below 12: ~1, 2, 10 deg and 33 deg for any rotation slower than 20 days

Slowly rotating Earth-air planets of a Sun-like star should need only ExoPlaSim's general repairs (untested; no run made); above 20 days ExoPlaSim's model day departs from the solar day unless the year holds ~12 rotations (64 d: 69.8 against 77.6 d; 243 d: 265 against 726 d)

Mars at 1 bar: H/R 0.00655 (5x Earth's), column 2.6x Earth's, g 0.38 of Earth's; Chapman factor 15.5; inside RRTMG's range at its 1-bar level; a breathable moon of a giant planet needs the downward infrared at the model top for the host's glow
Titan, present Mars and Venus lie outside PlaSim's and RRTMG's radiation and Morrison's water-only microphysics; the four limits of reach

In the NSSL runs hail does 82-88% of the charging and strikes ice and snow at 4.4-7.6 m/s; the deciding measurement is the sign rimed ice takes at 4-8 m/s in 0.02-0.2 g/m3 of cloud water at -5 to -16 C
374 of the 487 commits in Terluna's history to 186b294 carry a Claude Opus 5.5 co-author line
source: calc:git -C terluna log 186b294 --format=%b | grep -ci 'co-authored-by: claude opus 5.5' (374) against git log 186b294 --oneline | wc -l (487), run 2026-10-17

claims.text: ExoPlaSim at T21 runs a lunar model year in about 3.3-4.7 minutes on 4 MPI ranks, 20 years in roughly 70-95 minutes
The Sun clock was reported to ExoPlaSim's maintainers as issue #69 on 29 September 2026; the archived issue had no comments on 17 October 2026
With the gas bands, about 2 W/m2 of water's sunlight is still misplaced by layer, worth 0.19 K of ground in the middle-atmosphere column
The longwave-with-ice test extrapolates to balance at 306.8-307.1 K (the run ends at 306.77 K in year 19, warming 0.08 K a year); the figure's bars are window means against four baselines
Snow takes the drops' gravity exponent where its own laws give a larger one; 85% of falling water evaporates in the boxes and 57-73% in the rings

PlaSim's ten sigma levels, set for Earth's air, put the top three layers above 107 km, at 81-107 km and at 63-81 km, each spanning about 25 K, ice saturation changing 55-fold across the 81-107 km layer, and leave two layers for the lowest 6.5 km

The first calibration: the uncalibrated first design run passed 310 K and was still warming at 315.5 K in year 12 (A_uncalibrated); calibrated (run A) the same configuration settled at 295.5 K over years 30-39, at least 20 K cooler

In the rings forced from A28_dim5_moon, rain and cloud at a place change by a factor of several with the slice's direction, while temperature and wind agree within about a degree and 0.3 m/s between crossing rings

The reference's checks against other codes: PyRADS for water-only longwave at constant gravity, and a Monte Carlo Rayleigh reference to optical depth 1.5 (the lunar column reaches about 4 at 360 nm); no independent code checks its CO2, O2, collision-induced or solar calculation on the lunar column; the correlated-k emulation within 0.4-1.4 W/m2 of line-by-line OLR

ExoPlaSim's synchronous mode sets only NFIXED and FIXEDLON (__init__.py 2628-2630), keeping N = max(int(360/P/12+0.5),1)x12 and the model day P N/(N-1) from the rotation period (2616-2619; plasim.f90 1296-1300), so the convective-cover unit (rainmod.f90 1890) biases the cover by 0.125 ln(model day): +0.23 for TRAPPIST-1e's 6.1-day rotation, +0.31 for Proxima b's 11.2 days; the orbit default discards a configured obliquity and eccentricity in any run without fixedorbit
Swell that has outrun the local wind carries a third to two thirds of the wave energy on the lunar seas

By the design's own models the exobase stays at 142-198 K (below 200 K) behind the titania film and the air loses 0.61-1.4 kg/s over a solar cycle without magnets; at those rates the 1.2 atm atmosphere (2.84e18 kg) would take 64-148 billion years to remove
PlaSim's cloud tests from the Sun-and-tilt run: convective cover counted per 2,400 s (convective cloud near its floor) and the lowest layer's relative-humidity threshold lowered from 0.983 to 0.6

CCM3 cloud water counted at g_E with the mixing ratio scaled by g/g_E (ExoPlaSim patch 02); CM1's five soil layers 5-80 cm, 1.55 m in all (core patch 08); WRF-ELEC's flash log takes each channel's reach from the charge handed to the ions, where the released code logged it only above a charge threshold (A8)

Two-year test of the Sun and tilt alone from A28_dim5 (A28_dim5_sun_test, old split): clouds' effect in sunlight -15.7 -> -13.3 W/m2, planetary albedo 0.293 -> 0.285, global-mean surface 294.31 (years 15-24) -> 295.20 K over the two years (+0.9 K), top of the air still gaining 1.9 W/m2, rain 2.91 -> 2.74 mm/day; the step joined with the refit of the split settled at +0.59 K (A28_dim5_moon, years 20-29)
